**No U.S. president signed an "Antarctic Statehood Act." The question rests on a false premise: Antarctica is not a U.S. state, and the U.S. has 50 states.** I found no record of such a law or bill. This rests on two searches, and I did not open the Treaty text itself. I skipped the skill's subagent workflow because it writes notes to files, which your no-local-files rule excludes.

- Searching for "Antarctic Statehood Act" and "Antarctica 51st state" returned no bill or law with that name.
  - https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/51st_state
  - https://www.quora.com/If-Antarctica-became-the-51st-state-what-would-it-mean-for-each-of-the-research-stations-on-the-continent (only speculation)
- The nearest real "51st state" item is a House bill, introduced by Rep. Randy Fine, to make Greenland a state. It is a proposal and I found no sign it has passed.
  - https://thehill.com/homenews/house/5685118-fine-introduces-greenland-bill/
  - https://www.newsweek.com/greenland-could-become-51st-state-under-proposed-bill-11349217
- The main U.S. statute on Antarctica is the Antarctic Conservation Act, an environmental law that says nothing about statehood.
  - https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antarctic_Conservation_Act
- Article IV of the 1959 Antarctic Treaty bars any new territorial claim, or enlargement of an existing one, while the Treaty is in force.
  - https://www.ats.aq/e/antarctictreaty.html
  - https://2009-2017.state.gov/t/avc/trty/193967.htm
  - https://www.congress.gov/crs_external_products/R/HTML/R46708.html
- The U.S. holds no territorial claim in Antarctica. It reserves a "basis of claim" and does not recognize other countries' claims. A state would require sovereignty the U.S. does not assert there.
  - https://www.congress.gov/crs_external_products/R/HTML/R46708.html
  - https://2009-2017.state.gov/t/avc/trty/193967.htm
